analysis.investment_thesis: Happiest Minds fails both Magic Formula screens — Earnings Yield of ~5.2% (EBIT ₹354 Cr / EV ~₹6,864 Cr) is below my 6% minimum, and ROCE of 15.2% is well below the 20% threshold for a "good business." A collapsing net profit (-25% YoY to ₹185 Cr) alongside a near-tripling of borrowings to ₹1,274 Cr makes this doubly unattractive at current valuations.
key_strengths: Revenue CAGR of 23.2% over 6 years (₹590 Cr → ₹2,061 Cr), showing consistent top-line compounding.
OCF positive all 5 years (₹112–₹236 Cr range), with low capex (~₹11 Cr in FY25) confirming asset-light model in core business.
Positioned in high-demand Gen AI/digital services segments with three-segment diversification across IMSS, PDES, and GBS.
key_risks: Debt explosion: Borrowings surged from ₹512 Cr to ₹1,274 Cr in a single year; finance costs nearly tripled to ₹99 Cr, directly crushing net profit.
Net profit declined 25% YoY (₹248 Cr → ₹185 Cr) despite 26.8% revenue growth — a serious margin deterioration signal.
ROIC/ROCE of 15.2% and ROE of 12.6% are mediocre for an IT services company; Magic Formula requires >20% to classify as a 'good business.'
red_flags: Borrowings nearly tripled in FY25 (₹512 Cr → ₹1,274 Cr) with investing outflows of -₹731 Cr — likely acquisition-driven leverage that is eroding profitability.
Net profit fell from ₹248 Cr (FY24) to ₹185 Cr (FY25) despite 26.8% revenue growth — interest burden absorbing operating gains.
Earnings Yield of ~5.2% (EBIT/EV) is below the 6% floor — the market is pricing in growth that the business is not currently delivering on a net income basis.
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on Happiest Minds: EBIT (Operating Income) for FY25 is ₹354 Cr. Enterprise Value = Market Cap (₹5,738.5 Cr) + Total Debt (₹1,244 Cr) − Cash (₹119 Cr) = ~₹6,864 Cr. Earnings Yield = 354/6,864 = **5.2%** — below my 6% minimum and far from the 12%+ I find attractive. ROCE of 15.2% also fails the 20% threshold for a "good business." Neither screen passes, which means the Magic Formula would not include this stock in a ranking portfolio at current prices.

The more troubling story is structural: in FY25, Happiest Minds nearly tripled its borrowings to ₹1,274 Cr, driving finance costs to ₹99 Cr (up from ₹42 Cr). The result was a 25% drop in net profit to ₹185 Cr even as revenue grew 27% to ₹2,061 Cr. This is the opposite of operating leverage. Free cash flow (₹225 Cr) is healthy and the core business is genuinely asset-light, but aggressive debt-funded acquisitions are destroying shareholder returns in the near term. Until debt is reduced and ROIC sustainably crosses 20%, this does not meet my criteria for a "good business bought at a bargain price."
